transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
The children were killed yesterday in a shooting at an elementary school. The children were aged 5, 8, and 11 years old.
Another child and another teacher were wounded. Police in Bend say the shooter was a 16-year-old male.
He was shot and killed by a bystander who pursued him into the school.
NPR's Arazvut Rezvani says little is known about the bystander.
At a press conference last night, Oregon Governor Tina Kotek commended that bystander.
And to the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life, your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well.
It's not clear who the community member was, whether he was a parent or some armed passerby who sprang into action is not yet confirmed.
NPR's Arazvut Rezvani reporting. Vice President Vance rallied with Republicans in Michigan yesterday from the Michigan Public Radio Network, Colin Jackson has more.
Vance and several other Republicans are calling Michigan's election a choice between common sense and crazy.
It's been a common attack since Democrats won party nominations by campaigning on progressive policies like Medicare for All and stronger environmental protections.
Vance says Michigan is being tested.
The far left, the radicals of the Democratic Party, they're on the ascent.
This is not my papaw, it's the Democratic Party. This is not the party of JFK, it's not the party of Franklin Roosevelt, it's not even the party of Bill Clinton.
Democrats are accusing Republicans of making life worse for Michiganders by starting a war with Iran and a trade war with Canada.
Both topics Vance did not discuss during his speech.
For NPR News, I'm Colin Jackson in Michigan.
Saudi Arabia is postponing or canceling a slew of high profile events.
This move comes after Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen attacked Saudi Arabia's main airport in the capital, Riyadh.
NPR's Aya Batrawi reports this killed and injured scores of people over the past week.
A summit next week in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, between the European Union and leaders from six Gulf Arab states has been canceled.
The European Council did not give a reason why, but it comes after the suspension of flights at Riyadh airport following days of deadly Houthi attacks on passenger terminals.
Saudi Arabia has also canceled an international golf tournament slated for November, an electronic music festival, and pushed back a major tennis slam in Riyadh to the end of December.
And in its city of Jeddah, the Red Sea Film Festival and a star-studded Arab media awards show have also been postponed or canceled.
These events are important to Saudi Arabia's efforts to draw on tourists and investments.
Its war against the Houthis in Yemen, however, is threatening to derail those economic efforts.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
The protesters have issued high wind warnings for the area today.
Veterinary scientists working with California authorities say they know what caused the death of a popular bald eagle named Jackie.
The Internet-famous bird fell ill and died in August, even after getting care.
From member station KVCR, Madison Almond reports.
Veterinary pathologists at the San Diego Zoo concluded that Jackie died of a type of bird flu called highly pathogenic avian influenza.
They say it took a while to diagnose because she had unusual symptoms.
The strain of flu has been circulating in wild bird populations in the U.S.
Eagles may be exposed via contact with infected birds or eating infected prey.
Jackie's remains had to be cremated because bird flu is highly contagious.
The California Department of Fish and Wildlife says there's no evidence that Jackie's partner's shadow or their chicks were sick.
For NPR News, I'm Madison Almond in San Bernardino.
The Vatican says that Pope Leo's surgical recovery is progressing normally.
Leo has been in a Rome hospital since his Tuesday operation.
Doctors removed part of his right lung after discovering he had cancer.
Leo is participating in therapy, and the Vatican says he was able to help celebrate mass in the hospital yesterday.
You're listening to NPR.
That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A dot com. Code NPR.
